t: Section 110(b) of the Comprehensive Iran Sanctions, Accountability, and Divestment Act of 2010 (22 U.S.C. 8518(b)) is amended by striking “a report containing the matters” and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting the following: “a report, covering the 180-day period beginning on the date that is 30 days before the date on which the preceding report was required to be submitted by this section, that—“(1) contains the matters required in the report under subsection (a)(1); and“(2) identifies—“(A) the volume of crude oil and refined petroleum products imported to and exported from Iran (including through swaps and similar arrangements);“(B) the persons selling and transporting crude oil and refined petroleum products described in subparagraph (A), the countries with primary jurisdiction over those persons, and the countries in which those products were refined;“(C) the sources of financing for imports to Iran of crude oil and refined petroleum products described in subparagraph (A); and“(D) the involvement of foreign persons in efforts to assist Iran in—“(i) developing upstream oil and gas production capacity;“(ii) importing advanced technology to upgrade existing Iranian refineries;“(iii) converting existing chemical plants to petroleum refineries; or“(iv) maintaining, upgrading, or expanding existing refineries or constructing new refineries.”.

fable.w: This section only amends the required contents of a periodic federal report on Iran's petroleum trade and the foreign persons involved in it. The tempting reading is that references to "foreign persons" and "countries" bring outside parties in, but they are subjects of the report, not parties consulted before a federal decision. Nothing here provides for a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or a right to sue.
fable.s: a report, covering the 180-day period beginning on the date that is 30 days before the date on which the preceding report was required to be submitted by this section

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute to require the submission of a report containing specific data about oil imports and foreign persons. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties in the decision-making process. The mention of 'foreign persons' is descriptive of the data to be collected, not an invitation for them to participate in government decisions. Reporting requirements directed at Congress or internal agency records are considered internal government actions.
qwen_block.s: Section 110(b) of the Comprehensive Iran Sanctions, Accountability, and Divestment Act of 2010 (22 U.S.C. 8518(b)) is amended by striking “a report containing the matters” and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting the following: “a report, covering the 180-day period beginning on the date that is 30 days before the date on which the preceding report was required to be submitted by this section, that—“(1) contains the matters required in the report under subsection (a)(1); and“(2) identifies—“(A) the volume of crude oil and refined petroleum products imported to and exported from Iran (including through swaps and similar arrangements);“(B) the persons selling and transporting crude oil and refined petroleum products described in subparagraph (A), the countries with primary jurisdiction over those persons, and the countries in which those products were refined;“(C) the sources of financing for imports to Iran of crude oil and refined petroleum products described in subparagraph (A); and“(D) the involvement of foreign persons in efforts to assist Iran in—“(i) developing upstream oil and gas production capacity;“(ii) importing advanced technology to upgrade existing Iranian refineries;“(iii) converting existing chemical plants to petroleum refineries; or“(iv) maintaining, upgrading, or expanding existing refineries or constructing new refineries.”.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report identifies "foreign persons" and their activities, it involves outside parties. However, the section only mandates the creation and submission of a report by a federal official (implied by the context of amending a reporting requirement). It does not require consulting those foreign persons, nor does it grant them a role in the decision-making process. The identification of foreign actors is for informational purposes within a government report, not for participation.

opus.w: This amendment only changes what goes into a periodic report the executive branch must give Congress. Reports to Congress stay inside the federal government. The foreign persons, sellers, transporters and financiers are things the report must identify, not people who take part in a federal decision. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue.

opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The amendment names outside parties, such as "persons selling and transporting crude oil," "sources of financing" and "foreign persons." Those mentions could look like outside involvement. It fails because these parties are only things the report must identify. They don't consult with the government, sit on a panel, comment or sue. Section 110(b) of the Iran sanctions act requires a periodic report to Congress, so it stays inside the federal government.

The involvement of outside entities is limited to being the subject of the report's data, not participants in the decision-making process.
